Jheel is often used as a name for bodies of water in Hindu literature and mythology, such as Jheel Parvat, a hill in Rajasthan where the sage Markandeya performed his penance. The name evokes images of still, serene waters that reflect the tranquility and beauty of nature.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Jheel is associated with calmness, serenity, and a deep sense of inner peace. The name Jheel reminds us of the importance of calmness and peace in our lives and encourages us to strive for inner stillness in the midst of the chaos of the outer world.
